body: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, first released in Australia on 6 November 2013. A prisoner escort goes wrong, drawing the partners into a conflict involving dangerous beings from another dimension. The shorter adventure serves as an epilogue to the Future saga, returning to the established mixture of jumping, gadgets and extravagant weapons. Gravity provides its main variation, altering how a route is crossed and what direction a character can treat as the ground in a particular section.

Gravity-based gadgets allow Ratchet to reach places that would otherwise remain separated by empty space. The player reads the environment for possible connections rather than treating every gap as a jump. The arsenal also supplies comic new effects: the Winterizer turns enemies into snowmen, while the Nightmare Box distracts and frightens them. Such weapons change the character of a fight as well as dealing damage. Familiar improvements through use encourage another round with a newly obtained tool, even within a campaign built on a relatively compact scale.

Clank's Netherverses use two-dimensional layouts where changing gravity directs movement through a maze. A pursuing Nether must be guided toward the required exit, making the route and its timing the main problem. These sequences give Clank a separate activity while supporting the dimensional danger in Ratchet's story. Michael Bross composed the music, and reviewers generally praised the presentation and controls while noting the short length. Released near the end of the PlayStation 3 generation, Into the Nexus closed this part of the partners' journey before their later PlayStation adventures.
